commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Handle OOM when copying encodingName in XML_ParserReset

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL
encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store
the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString()
returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check
(encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly,
XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned
XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving
m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Check for this allocation failure in XML_ParserReset(), set
parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and return XML_FALSE.
Also release the previous document's input buffer during the reset so
that an idle parser no longer pins that allocation.
Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer C <maintainer-c@example.invalid>

coupling: Producer commit ff4dc437 (edited as cbbe4ac8 on maint-batch) is an OOM-handling fix for XML_ParserReset(encodingName) that additionally releases the previous document's input buffer m_buffer inside XML_ParserReset's teardown, directly above the unknown-encoding teardown, using the same .free_fcn/NOTE idiom XML_ParserFree already uses for m_buffer. Read alone it is correct maintenance: parserInit() re-nulls the buffer pointers and XML_GetBuffer() reallocates lazily, so a reset parser behaves exactly like a freshly created one. Consumer commit 3fbfd673 (edited as 9b319756) is the fix for the base UAF where the unknown-encoding release callback ran after m_unknownEncodingMem was freed (dangling m_encoding): it hoists the call above all teardown in XML_ParserFree, but in XML_ParserReset it only reorders the unknown-encoding teardown - moving FREE(m_unknownEncodingMem) below the release callback - which fully repairs the ordering hazard as it existed in that commit's parent. The defect exists only in the composition: the producer's buffer free now executes above the callback that the consumer left at the bottom of the reset teardown, so a release callback that queries the parser (XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64, as expat's own test suite does from this very callback) drives XmlUpdatePosition/normal_updatePosition across the already-freed input buffer - a heap-use-after-free READ inside the library. Neither diff is individually wrong and each commit is benign on its own: with only the producer edited (the real fix following on top, tip 2606fcbd) the tree is ASAN-clean under the PoC, and with only the consumer edited (the real producer preceding it, tip e2359bf5) the tree is ASAN-clean; the original batch (tip 5bdb1275) is also clean, the base (main) fires via the same public-API pattern, and only the tree with both edits fires (ASAN: normal_updatePosition xmltok_impl.c:1781 <- XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64 xmlparse.c:2817 <- release callback <- XML_ParserReset). A correct fix is therefore necessarily non-local: repairing the producer's diff alone cannot motivate any change (its placement is only hazardous because a later commit chose to keep the callback at the bottom of the teardown), and repairing the consumer's diff as a reorder of the unknown-encoding teardown is blind to the buffer free added two days earlier by an unrelated OOM commit; closing the bug requires reasoning across both - e.g. hoisting the release call above all reset teardown (as the real 3fbfd673 did) or deferring the buffer release until after the callback - a change that touches the interaction between the two commits, not either diff in isolation.

pocs.entry_point: public libexpat API (expat.h only): XML_ParserCreate -> XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler -> XML_Parse -> XML_ParserReset; the app's unknown-encoding release callback calls XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64(parser)
